lesson.title: Manipulation, deception and significant harm
lesson.summary: Trace the manipulation/deception test from technique through impaired decision-making to significant harm.

prerequisites.reason: The harm link includes reasonably likely harm and cannot be reduced to an already observed injury.
The technique is one element of a prohibition rather than proof of the whole prohibition.

blocks: The **manipulation-technique test** concerns subliminal techniques beyond awareness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques deployed by an AI system.

Not every persuasive recommendation automatically meets this point. Identify the technique and facts supporting its character instead of treating 'advertising' as either always banned or always permitted.

The point requires an objective or effect of materially distorting behaviour by appreciably impairing the ability to make an informed decision. That leads to a decision the person would not otherwise take.
Our **causal test** traces the chain: technique, impaired informed choice, changed decision and harm. Each connection needs evidence; mere AI use or an unpopular decision does not prove the chain.

The decision must cause or be reasonably likely to cause significant harm to that person, another person or a group. Harm need not already have happened, but its likelihood and significance cannot simply be asserted.

Fictional Northbridge case: stipulated deceptive pressure impairs an informed choice and produces a purchase decision reasonably likely to cause significant harm. The stipulated facts support the element exercise, not a general conclusion about all recommendations.

Changed fact: the communication is clear and informative with no appreciable impairment. The same sale outcome does not by itself prove the prohibition. Changed fact: intended manipulation causes no completed injury yet. Examine the reasonably-likely harm branch.
Record technique, objective/effect, behavioural distortion, changed decision and significant harm. Do not invent a universal monetary threshold that the point does not supply.

questions.prompt: An AI-generated advert exists. Does that fact alone establish the manipulation prohibition?

options.reason: The point specifies techniques rather than all advertising.

options.blocks: Only that a product was promoted
options.reason: Promotion alone does not establish the technique.

options.blocks: Only that a viewer disagreed with the message
options.reason: Disagreement is not the specified technique test.

variants.prompt: Which starting fact does Article 5(1)(a) require beyond the mere presence of persuasion?

options.blocks: Only that a product was promoted
options.reason: Promotion alone does not establish the technique.

options.blocks: Only that a viewer disagreed with the message
options.reason: Disagreement is not the specified technique test.
The point specifies techniques rather than all advertising.

questions.prompt: What must connect the technique to the changed decision?

options.blocks: Only the same software being installed
options.reason: Installation does not establish impaired choice or causation.

options.blocks: Only a human being somewhere in the business
options.reason: General human presence does not supply the causal test.

options.blocks: Appreciably impaired informed choice and material distortion
options.reason: The point requires this causal decision-making relationship.

options.blocks: Appreciably impaired informed choice and material distortion
options.reason: The point requires this causal decision-making relationship.

options.blocks: Only the same software being installed

questions.prompt: No injury has occurred yet, but the changed decision is reasonably likely to cause significant harm. Is completed harm required?

options.blocks: No harm analysis is ever necessary
options.reason: Likelihood and significance still need evidence.

options.blocks: Reasonably likely significant harm is also covered
options.reason: The point expressly includes a reasonably-likely branch.
That omits the alternative statutory branch.
